thesis: Meta is converting the largest consumer distribution network on earth (3.60 billion daily users) into an AI franchise: Q2 2026 revenue grew 28% to $60.8 billion on AI-driven ad ranking, Advantage+ crossed a $75 billion annual run rate, and the September 8 launch of the Muse personal agent hit 3.4 million downloads and the #1 US App Store spot. The cost of that pivot is extreme — 2026 capex guidance of $130-145 billion (vs $72.2 billion in 2025), Q2 free cash flow of just $784 million (-91% YoY), operating margin down to 31% from 43%, and buybacks suspended in H1 2026 while $24.9 billion of new debt was issued. The stock rallied ~30% in September to a $779.82 peak before pulling back on OpenAI's competing always-on agent, which leaves risk/reward balanced rather than compelling: HOLD, with accumulation better done on weakness toward the $600s than after a parabolic month.

financials.cash: $90.26B cash and marketable securities (vs $83.66B long-term debt)

drivers: Muse scales from launch hit to durable platform: the agent held the #1 US App Store rank with 3.4M+ downloads in three weeks, and Meta attaches commerce, travel and productivity monetization to a 3.6 billion-person funnel

Meta Enterprise Platform (launched September 28, 2026, led by ex-MongoDB CEO CJ Desai) turns internal AI capacity into third-party revenue; Zuckerberg says Meta is fielding compute-resale offers at a meaningful premium to cost and CFO Susan Li describes the company as demand constrained
Core advertising keeps compounding: Q2 impressions +14%, price per ad +12%, Advantage+ at a $75B annual run rate, 1M+ businesses using Meta Business Agents weekly

AI glasses become a real hardware franchise: 100+ styles across Ray-Ban, Oakley and Meta Glasses by end-2026, plus $1,299 Meta VR Glasses and the Muse Charm pendant, giving Meta an owned device channel for personal superintelligence

Custom MTIA silicon and the BlackRock El Paso 1GW venture lower the unit cost of the buildout — one sell-side estimate puts 2027 savings from in-house chips at ~$8.5B (bank estimate, not company-guided)

base_case.assumptions: Revenue growth decelerates from 28% toward the low-20s implied by the $61-64B Q3 2026 guide, full-year 2026 operating income finishes modestly above 2025's $83.3B as guided, capex lands in the middle of the $130-145B range and depreciation keeps margins near 30-35%, Muse monetization and the Enterprise Platform contribute revenue but not yet material profit, and the market pays roughly 7-8x forward revenue — consistent with the 57-analyst consensus target of ~$788-801

risks: OpenAI's 'o' always-on agent (unveiled at DevDay on September 29, 2026) commoditizes the Muse thesis that drove the entire September rally
Capex compounds into 2027 without proportional revenue: free cash flow stays near zero, buybacks remain suspended, and leverage rises from the current $83.7B of long-term debt
Depreciation and R&D (Q2 R&D was $21.7B, +67% YoY) keep operating margin in the low 30s or lower, so EPS declines even as revenue grows
Youth-safety litigation produces a material adverse judgment — Meta booked $2.40B of legal charges in Q2 and explicitly warns of possible material loss from US trials scheduled this year
Ad cycle turns or EU/US regulation constrains targeting, removing the growth that currently justifies the spend

catalysts.event: OpenAI DevDay 2026 keynote — formal unveiling of the 'o' always-on cloud agent, the most direct competitive read-through for Muse
Q3 2026 earnings — tests the $61-64B revenue guide, the first partial quarter of Muse engagement, and any monetization detail on the Meta Enterprise Platform
Sell-through of the Connect 2026 hardware slate: 100+ AI glasses styles, $1,299 Meta VR Glasses, Muse Charm pendant
Q4 and full-year 2026 results plus initial 2027 capex and expense guidance — the single largest swing factor for the free-cash-flow debate
US youth-related trials and regulatory proceedings; Meta has guided that outcomes may result in a material loss
MTIA custom-silicon deployment at scale and first revenue disclosure from compute resale / enterprise AI, the proof points for capex ROI

key_risks: Capex of $130-145B in 2026 against Q2 free cash flow of $784M — the buildout has already consumed nearly all operating cash flow and buybacks were suspended in H1 2026
OpenAI's competing always-on assistant directly attacks the Muse-driven re-rating that produced the ~30% September move
Margin compression from depreciation and R&D: operating margin fell to 31% in Q2 2026 from 43% a year earlier and net income declined 14% despite 28% revenue growth
Legal and regulatory exposure, including $2.40B of Q2 legal charges and company-flagged risk of material loss from US youth-safety trials
Reality Labs still loses ~$4.6B per quarter with only $431M of quarterly revenue, so the new hardware slate is a cost centre for now
Entry timing: the stock trades ~8% below its $779.82 52-week high after a parabolic month and ~14% above its 200-day moving average of $626.77
